extracted.intended_audience: prospective grant applicants and donors interested in EA infrastructure funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what the Effective Altruism Infrastructure Fund looks to support when recommending grants: the fund's mission, focus areas, types of projects, and high-level donor considerations. Useful for applicants shaping proposals and donors choosing to give to the fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core mission: increase impact via talent, capital, knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Effective Altruism Infrastructure Fund aims to increase the impact of projects that use the principles of effective altruism, by increasing their access to talent, capital, and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants should materially improve a project's access to one or more of these resources (talent, capital, knowledge) so that the project can increase its overall impact; proposals framed as multiplying impact via infrastructure are aligned with this mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reason and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Support projects that attempt to use reason and evidence to do as much good as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund has historically made strategic grants to incubate and grow projects that apply analytic or evidence-based approaches (e.g., research organisations, meta-charities, projects promoting EA in academia). Proposals should show how they rely on evidence/rational methods to increase impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directly increase exposure to EA principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Directly increase the number of people who are exposed to principles of effective altruism, or develop, refine or present such principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include outreach programs, courses, MOOCs, publications, podcasts, or other dissemination activities that expand awareness or understanding of EA ideas and thinking. Proposals should demonstrate reach and effectiveness of outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support recruitment of talented people
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the recruitment of talented people who can use their skills to make progress on important problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding may cover stipends, salaries, recruitment pipelines, or programs that attract and place high-impact talent; proposals should explain how supported people will lead to measurable progress on important problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a global EA community
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to build a global community of people who use principles of effective altruism as a core part of their decision-making process when deciding how they can have a positive impact on the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that strengthen national or regional EA groups, establish coworking spaces, run retreats, or otherwise grow sustainable, geographically diverse communities are within scope; show plans for community growth and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prioritization research
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct research into prioritizing between or within different cause areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is available for research that improves our understanding of cause prioritization or resource allocation (e.g., tools, models, papers). Proposals should explain methods, relevance to decision-making, and expected influence on funders or practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise funds or support other highly-effective projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise funds or otherwise support other highly-effective projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund may back meta-charities or platforms that fundraise for - or otherwise enable - highly effective direct-service organisations; proposals should show how fundraising/support activities will increase downstream impact and be cost-effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve community health and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve community health by promoting healthy norms for interaction and discourse, or assist in resolving grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants may target governance, norms development, mediation, or other interventions aimed at reducing harm and improving functioning within EA communities; describe mechanisms, expected outcomes, and how interventions will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of activities supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Support work that provides intellectual infrastructure for the effective altruism community, runs events, disseminates information, or fundraises for effective charities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists concrete activity types (intellectual infrastructure, events, dissemination, fundraising) and gives examples (MOOC, book, podcast, retreats, coworking). Applicants should map their activities to these types and provide evidence/metrics of effectiveness where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause scope (included causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: This includes a broad range of projects in global wellbeing (including animal welfare), longtermism, as well as cause-general work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund supports infrastructure work across multiple cause areas rather than only one cause; applicants should clarify how their project serves one or more of the listed cause domains and how it connects to EA priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic/incubation orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The fund attempts to make strategic grants to incubate and grow projects (including meta-charities, research organisations, and projects that promote EA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference appears to be for grants that are strategic (aimed at growth/incubation) rather than only funding routine operations; proposals should make the case for how the grant enables a strategic inflection or scaling opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of high-impact, rigorous grantmaking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund frames its mission around rigor and high impact; applicants should present clear impact logic, evidence, and reasoning for why the project will produce substantial positive effects relative to cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor considerations / reasons not to donate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons someone might choose not to donate: you don’t agree with the rationale for the Fund or the views of the Fund management team; concerns about conflicts of interest or grantmaker independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit transparency/expectation note for donors and applicants: disagreements with the fund's views or concerns about independence are valid reasons to avoid donating. Applicants should be aware of the fund's perspectives and potential conflict-of-interest scrutiny.
